questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The latest gadgets at a big technology show in Las Vegas
How robots are built in factories and tested for safety
Films about robots fighting humans and why people love them
Whether clever machines could one day take over the world
questions.why: Dan and Neil discuss the 'rise of the machines', the possible takeover of the world by AI.

questions.q: Why is Dan wearing protective gear and a helmet?
options: He has just been riding his bike to the studio
He is joking that he is ready for robots to take over
He is testing a new robot suit for the programme
He is going to a technology show after the recording
questions.why: Dan says he is 'getting ready for the inevitable rise of the machines'.

questions.q: What is David Hanson's ambition, according to the article?
options: To create an AI that can beat humans at any mental task
To build robots that can do all the housework at home
To stop AI becoming too clever for humans to control
To replace all air traffic controllers with machines
questions.why: Hanson said he wants to achieve an AI that can beat humans at any intellectual task.

questions.q: What example does Neil give of a job AI could do well?
options: Writing science fiction
Teaching children
Controlling air traffic
Driving taxis
questions.why: Neil mentions air traffic control, saying there would never be another plane crash.

questions.q: Why does Neil mention Isaac Asimov?
options: He wrote the first play about robots
He built the first sentient robot
He predicted robots would take over by 2020
He created laws to stop robots acting against people
questions.why: Neil says Asimov came up with three laws every robot must follow to stop it acting against humanity.

questions.q: What does Dan fear an AI made to protect humanity might do?
options: Take control of everything we do, so we lose our freedom
Start wars between countries to reduce the population
Refuse to follow orders and switch itself off for good
Leave Earth to find other intelligent life in space
questions.why: Dan imagines it controlling everything to stop us hurting each other, so we'd lose our freedom.

questions.q: What does Sam from the Learning English team think?
options: It could easily happen very soon
It's possible, but technology will reach its limit first
It will never happen, and humans would win anyway
Only films make people think about it
questions.why: Sam says 'never in a million years' because we'd programme them and beat them anyway.

questions.q: Who in the Learning English team agrees most with Dan's worry?
options: Phil
Kee
Sam
Neil
questions.why: Kee says she totally thinks it could happen once a robot can think for itself.
